title: Exegesis of Proverbs
english: The Lord will not starve to death a righteous soul; but he will overturn the life of the impious. If the life of the impious is wickedness, the Lord will overturn this, so that the impious will clearly be seen at some time to be not impious; for after this overturning, the Lord will hand over the kingdom to God and Father, so that God may become 'all in all'.
Instruction preserves the paths of life; but instruction wanders uncontrolled. He calls uncontrolled instruction the bad political order of the soul, which becomes a stranger to it through wandering.

Righteous lips cover enmity; but those who bring forth reviling are thoughtless. He says enmity is wickedness; for through this we become enemies of God. 'For if we were enemies,' says Paul, 'we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son.' If enmity is wickedness, then friendship is virtue and knowledge is that of God, through which we become friends of God and of the holy powers; for upon this friendship, those who are his friends are also friends to one another.
Desire is acceptable to the righteous; 'Lord, all my desire is against you,' says David.

The fear of the Lord adds days; but the years of the impious will be diminished. If 'the fear of the Lord adds days' and 'the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom', these days are parts of wisdom being made under the sun of righteousness, for which David also prays, saying, 'do not bring me up in the midst of my days.' And having fulfilled these days, Abraham died, concerning whom it is said, 'and Abraham died old and full of days.'

The righteous will not possess the age; but the impious will not inhabit the land. Instead of the age, and Paul says, 'I will not eat meat for ever, so that I may not scandalize my brother,' he calls the age the duration accompanying the constitution of his life.
The lips of righteous men send forth grace; but the mouth of the impious turns away. The mouth has now set the mind.

Salvation exists in much counsel for those who have no governance and fall like leaves, being carried about by every wind of teaching and shipwrecked regarding faith. The evil one does evil when he mixes with the righteous; but he hates the tone of security, those concerning salvation.
A man of mercy does good to his soul, but the merciless man drives the body out of it. Here the soul is spoken against by the body.

And Christ in the Gospels calls the soul 'body', saying, 'the eye is the lamp of the body' (Matt 6:22). Having said lamp, he means the intellect—for it is the receiver of knowledge—but 'body' refers to the spirited and desiring part of the soul, which some call the irrational part and others the passionate part.

He who strikes hand against hand unjustly shall not be unpunished; but he who sows righteousness shall receive a reward of the faithful. This one who strikes hand against hand unjustly is the teacher of evil deeds and dogmas. And this one who sows righteousness is the one who puts forward words concerning virtues and the knowledge of God.

There are those who, sowing their own, make more; and there are those who, gathering, are diminished. Those who sow their own and make more are opposed by those who gather and are diminished. If those who sow their own are those who sow into the spirit and reap life, those who gather are those who sow into the flesh and gather corruption to themselves.

He who withholds grain would leave it to the nations; but a blessing is upon the head of the giver. This is similar to that which is said by our Savior in the Gospels: 'No one, after lighting a lamp, puts it under a bushel, but on a lampstand, and it shines for all those in the house' (Matt 5:15).

If the work of making is a work of good things, and the work of virtues is a practical work, then the practical work is the making. The tree of life grows from the fruit of righteousness; but untimely souls are removed by lawlessness. This tree of life is the one planted in the midst of paradise, which Adam is prevented from grasping after the sin, having cast away the seeds of righteousness, from which the tree of life grows.

He who finds grace is greater, but the lawless man shall be passed over in silence: 'Do not pass me over from you, says David, lest I become like those descending into the pit' (Ps 88:49). The good man shall inherit sons of sons; but wealth is stored up for the ungodly.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Scholia on Proverbs
english: The wickedness of the ungodly. But the righteous will consume it, clearly through good teaching, whether now or in the future age, over fifteen cities.
And Paul says: 'But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and the revelation of the righteous judgment of God' (Rom 2:5).

All things are contrary to a foolish man; but the lips of the wise are weapons of perception. For 'it does not oppose' wisdom 'anything evil,' because it is an invincible weapon; for the demons are only powerless against it.

The houses of the foolish must undergo cleansing; but the houses of the righteous are receptive, so that having become pure, they may see God; for this is the blessed end which is preserved for all rational nature.

The reckless man will be filled with his own ways; but a good man [is known] from his thoughts. Regarding thoughts, he has now spoken of the states of virtues, just as he set them in opposition to the ways of the reckless.

The foolish are divided by wickedness; but the cunning will prevail through perception. He set wickedness in opposition to perception. If wickedness opposes virtue, then perception now signifies virtue.

In increasing righteousness there is much strength; but the ungodly are uprooted from the earth. 'Unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven' (Matt 5:20).

The education of the inattentive is known by those passing by; but let those who hate reproof perish shamefully. Regarding reproof, he has now spoken of the commandments; for these reprove us when we are sinning.
All the time the eyes of the evil receive evil; but the good are at rest always. Silence is a refuge from wickedness.
Ways of life are the thoughts of the prudent, so that having turned away from Hades, he may be saved. Regarding ways of life, he speaks of the practical virtues which lead toward knowledge.

The ways of righteous men are acceptable to the Lord; and through them, even enemies become friends. This is from Paul preaching: 'Those who were once enemies were reconciled to God through the death of His Son'; however, one must take care whether all enemies become friends through the righteous, so that Christ might also say to all: 'I no longer call you slaves, but friends' (John 15:15).
Divination is upon the lips of a king; but in judgment, [one] will not wander...

Christ is the Searcher of Hearts who will judge the inhabited world with justice by his mouth (Prov 14:5). The wrath of a king is a messenger of death (Prov 14:27), but a wise man will escape him. The angel who stands regarding matters of punishment is called the wrath of God.
Diseases of wisdom are better than gold (Prov 14:34), but diseases of prudence are better than silver. Knowledge of wisdom is better than gold, but knowledge of prudence is better than silver.
He who receives instruction will be in good things (Prov 15:33), but he who guards reproofs will be a sophist. Reproofs refers to the commandments of God; for these reprove us when we are sinning.

A fountain of life is a concept to those who possess it, but instruction is bad for the foolish. The uncontrollable instruction, the foolish have now named it instruction. If the instruction of the foolish is evil, the uncontrollable instruction is foolishness.
The heart of a wise man will understand things from his own mouth (Prov 14:10); but he will carry epistemic-knowledge upon his lips. Knowledge said epistemic-knowledge to mean knowing all things.

A crooked man sends out evils and flashes the spark of deceit (Prov 14:13), separating friends. The Word attempts to teach the demons, learning from the devil, to attempt to act against the saints and to test them, separating them from the knowledge which is natural for uniting them to the heavenly powers. Solomon, as I think, revealed this very thing through this proverb, calling Satan a crooked man, flashing the sparks of deceit the evil demons, instead of being taught, and the saints, the friends joining one another through knowledge.
He who supports his eyes is reckoned straying, but he defines all evils with his lips; this is a furnace of evils. The spirit of a driving wind scatters the flame of this furnace.

Everything comes into the laps of the unrighteous (Prov 14:32), but all things just are from the Lord (Prov 14:32). It should be noted that he spoke of the hearts of the unrighteous as laps here. I think also that everywhere 'lap' signifies either the mind or knowledge. If it is also a deceptive lap, it will signify ignorance.

title: Virtue as a Shield and the Nature of True Friendship
english: Having turned away from evil and having prevailed through virtues, he has mastered foolish demons. And such a person will become also a steward of the mysteries of God, giving spiritual knowledge to each of the brothers according to the analogy of their state, sometimes watering the Corinthian with milk, sometimes feeding the Ephesian with firmer food, discussing height and length and breadth and depth, and through these dimensions signifying the division of the logical nature, which contains the discourses concerning the judgment and providence of God, being most profound and fleeing the human condition.

Just so Jesus son of Nun distributed the land of promise to the twelve tribes, which is a symbol of the knowledge of God and of those things having come from Him. However, it must be known that the discourses concerning the incarnation of Christ and His appearance in Judah are held in reserve for knowledge; for in this lot Christ is born. But I consider the discourses concerning providence to be fitting for the state of the hidden Judah and Benjamin, whose names I regard as distinctions of different and pure states, if Judah is interpreted as confessing, and Benjamin as a son of days or a son of the right hand.

An evil man obeys the tongue of the lawless; but a righteous man does not give heed to lying lips. This one obeys the tongues of the lawless, he who receives from them thoughts and hastens to act according to them, whereas the righteous is said not to give heed, that is, not to nourish them any further within himself.

To the faithful belongs the whole world of things; to the unfaithful, not even a mite. The faithful, he says, will see the discourses of this world, which he has figuratively gathered as riches of the mind; but the unfaithful will not know the discourse of even a chance matter because of the impurity of his soul. Since knowledge of God is a wealth of the soul, Paul teaches this through those things in which he writes, 'you were enriched in every way in all knowledge and all wisdom' (Colossians 2:3). And if anyone wishes to show that this is not the meaning of this proverb, let him say where those who passed through became destitute of things, 'in meager things, in skins of goats, being poorly treated, afflicted, and lacking' (2 Corinthians 11:3); and how also the un-
He will not have a single penny, being surrounded by the wealth of many unfaithful ones, I say, many kings and rulers of this world.

Faithful lips do not suit a fool, nor false lips a righteous man: 'For what fellowship has righteousness with lawlessness, or what communion light with darkness?' (2 Cor 6:14). He who hides wrongdoings seeks friendship; but he who hates hiding distinguishes friends and kinsmen. Through righteousness we hide injustice, through self-control we hide intemperance, again through love we hide hatred, and through freedom from greed we hide avarice. We also hide pride through humility and boldness through meekness, seeking the spiritual friendship, which signifies holy knowledge. And according to Paul, some of the saints are said to have become fellow-citizens and kinsmen of Jerusalem, 'having been built up on the foundation of the apostles and prophets' (Eph 2:20).

He who gives evil instead of good, evil shall not move out from his house. If he who gives evil instead of evil is lawless, how much more the one who gives evil instead of good is more lawless? Such became toward God the Israel of the wilderness, to whom Moses says in Deuteronomy: 'These generations are crooked and perverse, repaying the Lord' (Deut 32:5).

Authority is given by words, the beginning of righteousness; but standing and strife precede need. Knowledge follows righteousness; but wickedness precedes ignorance. He who judges the unrighteous as righteous, and the righteous as unrighteous, is unclean and an abomination before God. Similar is he who calls the bitter sweet and the sweet bitter, and calls the light darkness and the darkness light.

Why did money exist for a fool? For he will not be able to acquire wisdom without a heart. Money belongs to a fool; for regarding each of his matters, there is foolishness; because of these things, having become without a heart, he is unable to acquire wisdom.

He who makes his own house lofty seeks destruction; but he who turns aside from learning will fall into evils. 'He who turns aside from learning,' because 'the Lord opposes the proud' (Prov 16:5), 'will fall into evils' (Prov 24:21). Let a friend be to you at all times; but brothers are useful in necessities.
